analysis.investment_thesis: AvenuesAI is a near-debt-free payments business growing revenue strongly, but paper-thin margins (3.23% operating), anemic ROE of 6.47%, and promoter holding of just 27.29% make this fundamentally unacceptable by my standards. I will not own a business where the founder has so little skin in the game and returns on capital are so poor.
key_strengths: Near-zero leverage: D/E of 0.02 with INR 331 Cr cash — balance sheet is clean
Revenue CAGR of 31.6% over 9 years with net profit growing from INR 9 Cr to INR 236 Cr
Attractive valuation multiples: P/B 1.06x and P/S 0.78x suggest no speculative premium
key_risks: Promoter holding at only 27.29% — far below my 55% floor; management skin-in-the-game is insufficient
ROE of 6.47% and ROCE of 8.65% are deeply inadequate — a business this size should earn far more on equity
FCF turned sharply negative in 2025 (-INR 304 Cr) as capex surged to INR 376 Cr — cash conversion is broken
red_flags: Promoter stake at 27.29% — well below my 55% minimum, signals weak founder conviction
Operating margin of 3.23% — payments should be high-margin at scale; this is a structural weakness
Volatile OCF: swung from INR 720 Cr (2024) to just INR 72 Cr (2025) — earnings are not reliably converting to cash
Company rebranded to 'AvenuesAI' in January 2026 — smells of AI-hype branding, not business substance
Other income of INR 71 Cr is 30% of net profit in 2025 — earnings quality is questionable
analysis.detailed_analysis:
AvenuesAI operates in digital payments (CCAvenue) and e-commerce software — a competitive, commoditising space requiring constant reinvestment. Revenue has grown impressively from INR 337 Cr (2016) to INR 3,993 Cr (2025), but this growth has not translated into acceptable returns. ROE of 6.47% and ROCE of 8.65% are below what I earn in a fixed deposit — there is no point deploying capital in a business that cannot earn its cost of equity. The operating margin of 3.23% tells me this is a low-moat, price-competitive payments processor, not a toll-booth business.

The balance sheet is the one genuine positive — D/E of 0.02 with INR 331 Cr cash is exactly what I like. But the 2025 cash flow picture concerns me deeply: capex of INR 376 Cr produced negative FCF of INR 304 Cr while net profit was INR 236 Cr. The business is investing heavily in infrastructure (CWIP peaked at INR 311 Cr in 2024), yet operating leverage is not materialising in margins. The promoter holding of 27.29% is disqualifying — I need promoters who own majority of what they have built. The "AI" rebrand is marketing noise. This is not the quiet, steady compounder I seek.
